claims.statement: The real native client sent the supplied synthetic API key in a JSON POST to the ima add_model service.
claims.status: observed in source, controlled local execution, and real native TLS application bytes
limits: The live experiment uses a synthetic no-permission marker; does not establish a real-key breach.
Does not establish server storage, retention, access control, or a breach.

claims.statement: The inspected frontend preserves slash-containing model names.
claims.status: observed in source, controlled local execution, and real request JSON
limits: No public-endpoint backend A/B test; separate server name rules remain possible.

claims.statement: The local Magpie gateway accepted group/deepseek-v4-1-flash and replied OK.
limits: One point-in-time gateway test, not an ima-server compatibility test.

claims.statement: A cloud validation path cannot reach the user computer through its own 127.0.0.1 address. This is a plausible explanation of the save failure.
claims.status: architecture-based inference; exact failure branch unobserved
limits: Server may reject loopback, fail to connect, impose protocol/name rules, or take another branch.
Generic UI validation error is not a model-character error code.

claims.statement: Inspected chat code sends question and model identity to the ima assistant service; official privacy text discloses AI content cloud processing.
claims.status: client-source observation and official policy statement; backend delegation remains an inference
limits: Policy statement does not establish API key storage details.

claims.statement: Real native-client add_model request and response JSON were reconstructed from captured HTTP/2 DATA frames.
claims.status: observed real native TLS application data
limits: The initial Default-mode log has metadata only; the separately authorized Everything-mode log supplies DATA bytes.
Original logs stay private; published DATA frames independently reconstruct the benign request/response but cannot independently authenticate original log provenance.
NetLog is client network-stack logging, not a physical network packet capture; HTTPS was not disabled.

claims.statement: In the observed failed-save flow, an outgoing collect telemetry body contained the same complete request parameter, including the synthetic API key.
claims.status: observed in real outgoing TLS application data
limits: One observed synthetic-key failure flow; not a claim about every configuration or version.
Full telemetry payload stays private; the public excerpt omits account identifiers, headers, trace values and other messages.
Does not establish telemetry retention, access control, or a real-key breach.
